parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
Benzene can be converted into cyclohexane.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: For this reaction name the type of reaction and identify the reagent and conditions needed.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
State the bond angles in benzene and cyclohexane.

Explain your answers.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
When benzene reacts with $\text{SO}_3$, benzenesulfonic acid is produced.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

The mechanism of this reaction is similar to that of the nitration of benzene. Concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is used in an initial step to generate the $\text{SO}_3\text{H}^+$ electrophile as shown.
$$\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{SO}_3\text{H}^+ + \text{HSO}_4^-$$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Draw a mechanism for the reaction of benzene with $\text{SO}_3\text{H}^+$ ions. Include all necessary curly arrows and charges.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation to show how the $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ catalyst is reformed.

parts.label: (c)
(d)
parts.stem:
When concentrated sulfuric acid is added to water, dissociation takes place in two stages.
stage 1 $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{HSO}_4^-$
stage 2 $\text{HSO}_4^- \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{SO}_4^{2-}$ $K_{\text{a}2} = 1.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$

$K_{\text{a}2}$ is the acid dissociation constant for stage 2.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Write the expression for the acid dissociation constant $K_{\text{a}2}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is considered a strong acid whereas $\text{HSO}_4^-$ is considered a weak acid.

Suggest how the magnitude of the acid dissociation constant for stage 1 compares to $K_{\text{a}2}$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Benzoic acid, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, is a weak acid. A solution of $0.0250\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ benzoic acid has a pH of 2.90.

Calculate the $K_{\text{a}}$ of benzoic acid.
